events.title: The New Kingdom in Egypt
events.description: Egypt expels the Hyksos and enters its most powerful period. The pharaohs expand the empire to Nubia in the south and Syria in the north.

events.title: Hatshepsut – Female Pharaoh
events.description: Hatshepsut rules as pharaoh of Egypt for over 20 years. She is known for her peaceful trade and grand building projects, including the temple at Deir el-Bahri.

events.title: Thutmose III – "Egypt's Napoleon"
events.description: Thutmose III conducts 17 military campaigns and expands the Egyptian empire to its greatest extent, all the way to the Euphrates.

events.title: The Amarna Letters
events.description: Over 300 diplomatic clay tablets found in Akhetaten show correspondence between Egypt and the city-states of Canaan. Some letters mention the "Habiru" people causing unrest in Canaan.

events.title: Akhenaten and Monotheism
events.description: Pharaoh Akhenaten introduces the worship of one god, Aten (the sun disk), and bans the traditional gods. The first known attempt at monotheism by a head of state in history.

events.title: Tutankhamun
events.description: The young pharaoh Tutankhamun restores the traditional religion after Akhenaten's reforms. His nearly intact tomb was discovered in 1922.

events.title: The Hittite Empire
events.description: The Hittite Empire reaches its peak power and controls large parts of Anatolia and Syria. They are one of Egypt's greatest rivals.

events.title: The Battle of Kadesh
events.description: Ramses II of Egypt fights the Hittites in one of antiquity's largest battles. It results in the world's first known peace treaty.

events.title: Ramses II the Great
events.description: Ramses II reigns for 66 years and is Egypt's most famous pharaoh. He builds enormous monuments, including the Abu Simbel temples. Many scholars link him to the Exodus pharaoh.

events.title: Merneptah Stele
events.description: Pharaoh Merneptah's victory stele from c. 1208 BC contains the earliest known reference to "Israel" outside the Bible.

events.title: Trojan War
events.description: The mythical/historical war between Greek city-states and Troy in northwest Anatolia. Immortalized in Homer's Iliad.

events.title: Late Bronze Age Collapse
events.description: A catastrophic system collapse strikes the entire eastern Mediterranean region. Several great empires fall, cities are burned, and trade networks break down. The cause is likely a combination of the Sea Peoples, drought, earthquakes, and internal revolts.

events.title: Ugaritic Texts
events.description: The city of Ugarit in Syria leaves behind rich archives with religious texts about Canaanite religion: Baal, El, Anat, and Mot. Important for understanding the biblical context.

events.title: Mycenaean Civilization
events.description: The Mycenaean civilization dominates Greece with fortified cities such as Mycenae and Tiryns, and a bureaucratic system using Linear B script.
